title: Ferromagnetic Bare Metal Stent for Endothelial Cell Capture and Retention
protocol: Make an extruded hollow cylinder by selecting on ‘extruded boss/base’ feature with the wall thickness equal to the stent strut thickness.
Design a stent pattern on a different sketch plane tangential to the extruded cylinder.
Make the width of the flat pattern to match the circumference of the extruded hollow cylinder.
Transfer the flat pattern design onto the hollow cylinder using the wrap feature.
Save the part in its native format and also in ACIS format to be exported for FEA.
Import the solid geometry saved in ACIS format into the part module of the FEA software for further analysis.
Model 2 analytical cylinders coaxially to the stent in the part modeler of the FEA software.
The outer cylinder has an initial diameter larger than the diameter of the stent to simulate the crimper and the inner cylinder has an initial diameter of 1 mm to simulate a balloon for inflation.
Double click on the ‘instances’ tree item of the assembly modeler to assemble the above said parts in relative positions.
Use the mesh module of the FEA software, specify the element type as 20-node hexahedral element with reduced integration, specify the element size, and mesh the stent.
Specify frictionless rigid contact pairs between the stent and the two cylinders respectively in the ‘interaction properties’ of the model tree.
Assign elasto-plastic stress-strain behavior of 2205 stainless steel to the stent model.
Define boundary conditions to crimp the outer cylinder to 1 mm.
Remove the outer cylinder to simulate relaxation of the crimped stent.
Expand the inner cylinder to 3 mm to simulate expansion.
Remove the inner cylinder to simulate recoil of the stent.
Define simulation parameters including number of processors and RAM allocated in the ‘Analysis’ model tree item.
Run the simulation.
Open the result file (filename.odb) and post-process the results.
Study principal strains from the results.
Iteratively improve the stent design to achieve a principal strain of 20% which is less than the failure limit of the material.
Obtain 2205 stainless steel tubes by gun drilling and precision grinding bar stock material at a precision machining company.
Transfer the precision ground tubes and flat pattern stent design to a stent cutting company for laser cutting and electropolishing.
Passivate the surface of electropolished stents by submersing them in 50% HCl for 10 min.
Submerge the stents in a base solution of 10% NaHCO3 for another 10 min.
Wash the stents with ethyl alcohol.
Rinse the stents with deionized water.
Crimp the stent onto a trifold balloon using a hand held crimping tool.
Hold the stent and trifold balloon in the crimping tool.
Press the handle to radially deform the stent for crimping on the balloon.
Inspect the crimped stent using a microscope for uniform crimping and signs of failure.
Expand the stent to the designed diameter of 3 mm by pressurizing the trifold balloon with water.
Examine the expanded stents for microscopic fractures and uniform expansion.
Magnetize the stents diametrically or axially using a strong neodymium magnet.
Hold the stent on one flat face or next to the cylindrical surface for magnetization.
Mount the stents individually onto glass mandrels.
Position the glass mandrels in the precision chuck of the magnetic probing fixture.
Place the magnetic microsensor probe close to the stent using XYZ stages assembly.
Measure the baseline reading of the magnetic microsensor far away from the stent.
Measure the retained magnetic field at the stent's surface by positioning the probe using the XYZ stages.
Derive endothelial outgrowth cells (EOC) from porcine peripheral blood.
Culture EOC in a T-75 flask until approximately 80% confluent.
Incubate derived EOC with SPION at a concentration of 200 μg/ml for 16 hours at 37°C.
Aspirate the cell culture medium gently.
Gently wash the cells by adding 10 ml of phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) to the flask, rocking, and aspirating the PBS.
Stain the cells with fluorescent dye (CM-DiI) for visualizing during experiments as per manufacturer’s instructions.
Add the dye to 10 ml of cell culture medium at a concentration of 5 µl/ml and incubate with the cells for 30 min at 37 °C.
Wash the cells with PBS as in step 4.1.4.
Incubate with 3 ml of 0.25% trypsin-EDTA solution for 5 min at 37 °C to lift the cells from the flask.
Transfer the cell suspension to a 15 ml conical tube, top off with PBS, and centrifuge at 500 x g for 5 min to form a cell pellet.
Re-suspend the cell pellet in PBS at a concentration of 1-2x10^6 cells/ml.
Mix thoroughly by pipetting in and out of the conical tube several times.
Design and fabricate (e.g., 3D printing) a simple fixture to hold the stent just above the surface of a glass coverslip.
Demagnetize a stent using an electromagnetic degausser or magnetize a stent diametrically or axially using a strong neodymium magnet.
Pipette the SPION-labeled EOC suspended in PBS into the dish containing the axially magnetized or diametrically magnetized or non-magnetized control stents.
Image the stents with EOC suspended in PBS immediately for fluorescence using an inverted fluorescence microscope.
Draw peripheral blood from 4 healthy Yorkshire pigs weighing approximately 50 kg, 3 weeks prior to stent implantation.
Administer anti-platelet medication starting 3 days before surgery with aspirin 325 mg and clopidogrel 75 mg daily.
Anesthetize the pigs with intramuscular Telazol, Xylazine, and Atropine (5/2-3/0.05 mg/kg respectively).
Intubate the pig and place it on inhalation of 1-2.5% Isoflurane anesthesia.
Shave the ventral neck region of the pig.
Access the right carotid artery with a 9 French sheath.
Cannulate the target coronary artery and inject iodinated contrast dye to obtain fluoroscopic images.
Place a 0.014 inch standard coronary guidewire in the artery.
Advance the balloon and stent using this guide wire.
Deploy the stent in a 3-3.5 mm diameter vessel.
Occlude the blood flow within the RCA proximal to the implanted stents using an over-the-wire balloon.
Deliver approximately 2x10^6 autologous EOC labeled with SPION suspended in 4 ml of PBS via the central catheter over a 2 min period.
Restore blood flow to the RCA after 2 min of additional occlusion.
Transfer the animal to the recovery room.
Closely monitor the animal until it has regained consciousness.
Administer anti-platelet medication (aspirin 325 mg and clopidogrel 75 mg) post-operatively until sacrifice.
Euthanize the animals 7 days after surgery by first anesthetizing the animal.
Administer intravenously a lethal dose of sodium pentobarbital (100 mg/kg).
Surgically harvest the stented arterial segments.
Fix the explanted arteries in 10% formalin buffer for a minimum of 30 min.
Leave the samples in formalin buffer for further histological analysis.
Outsource the fixed sample to facilities capable of performing histology with metal stents.
Embed the samples in methylmethacrylate.
Cross-section the samples.
Analyze the samples histologically using Mallory’s staining technique with Prussian blue stain for iron particles.
